COURSES CASC Bill 2025-2026-04A At the January 6, 2026 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. INFORMATIONAL MATTERS COURSES FORWARD TO THE GRADUATE COUNCIL FOR REVIEW: BUS401 | Global Topics in Business: Career Accelerator JOR490 | Community News Lab FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: INE347 | Entrepreneurial Accounting and Finance, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Topics focus on the principles of new venture accounting and finance. Accounting topics include assessing the health of a new venture, and cash and other financial planning for the smaller enterprise. Finance topics include introduction to start u p issues such as raising seed and growth capital from founders, grants, venture capitalists and angels, investment banking, commercial banking, bootstrapping sources, entrepreneurship through acquisition, and understanding audiences of financial statements and issues unique to small and medium-sized firms. We will also investigate sources of new venture support found both locally and nationally. (Lec. 3) Pre: Junior standing. COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDC475 | Early Childhood Practical Teaching Residency 1 Seminar, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) This seminar course offers professional support for the early Childhood Practical teaching Residency. This includes dialogue, reflection, goal setting, and teaching analysis during fall residency

and is conducted by a clinical educator and a university supervisor.
Focus will be on developing practices in classroom and behavior management, and assessment to meet the needs of a diverse range of learners, and to help students become reflective and intentional early childhood educators. (Lec. 2, Seminar 1) Pre: Concurrent enrollment in EDC350 and EDC474, admission to College of Education; Admission to the Early Childhood Certification Program; Admission to the Early Childhood Care and Education for Working Professionals; or permission of the instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: BIO380 | The Ecology of Iceland and the North Atlantic, effective Summer 2026 (3 crs.) Survey of North Atlantic coastal and oceanic habitats via field experience in Iceland, with emphasis on ecology and fisheries.
Travel required; additional costs apply. (Lec. 3) Pre: BIO260 or BIO262, or by permission of instructor GEO380 | Geology of Iceland, effective Summer 2026 (3 crs.) Explores physical geology in an off-campus field experience in Iceland with a focus on sustainable geosciences in a changing climate.

Travel required; additional costs apply. (Lec. 1, Seminar) Pre: 200-level course in GEO or permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF NURSING: NUR200 | Nurse Wellbeing & Resilience, effective Fall 2026 (1 cr.) Introduces nursing students to wellness and resiliency concepts emphasizing self-care, stress management, emotional intelligence, and mindfulness to promote personal well-being, professional balance, and sustainable nursing practice through reflective, evidence-based learning. (Lec. 1) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.
NUR204 | Pathopharmacology I, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Examine pathophysiology and pharmacology principles for nurses, emphasizing concepts and rationales essential for clinical decision-making and the care of individuals with select diseases across the lifespan. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.

NUR205 | Pathopharmacology II, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Examine pathophysiology and pharmacology principles for nurses, emphasizing concepts and rationales essential for clinical decision-making and the care of individuals with select diseases across the lifespan, part B. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a mi nimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.
NUR458 | Comprehensive Care Across the Lifespan & Settings, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Care of individuals and families across the lifespan and settings with complex illnesses, emphasizing client and family responses, empowering self-care, and maximizing quality of life. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR333, NUR334, NUR353, NUR354 and NUR413.
Not for graduate credit,

COURSE MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: ART243 | Sculpture I: Making the Object, effective Fall 2026 Change credits, prerequisites, title (4 crs.) Formation of three-dimensional forms employing basic sculptural materials and techniques.
Basic media, emphasis on form, material, and structural means in studio practice. (Studio) ART315 | Photography II: Contemporary Photography Practice, effective Fall 2026 Change title, credits, description, prerequisites, repeat criteria (4 crs.) Expand your photography skills to visually communicate creatively through photography and imaging while engaging with contemporary practices.
Photo II emphasizes experimentation, printing and installation. (Studio) Pre: ART214.
May be taken up to two times.
ART332 | Print Media II: Contemporary Print Practice, effective Fall 2026 Change title, description, repeat criteria, prerequisites (4 crs.) Students expand printmaking through relief, monotype, bookmaking, risograph, and digital methods while engaging global print cultures and contemporary practices. (Studio) Pre: ART231.
May be repeated for up to 8 credits.

JOR445 | Special Topics in Journalism, effective Fall 2026 Change repeat criteria (3 crs.) Subject, course content, and years offered will vary according to expertise and availability of instructors. (Lecture/Lab./Seminar) Pre: permission of instructor.
May be repeated for credit with different topic, up to 5 times.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: BAI109 | Business Computing and Quantitative Analysis, effective Fall 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Applications, concepts, and skills relevant to technology and quantitative processes in business.
Topics include financial analysis, business modeling, and spreadsheets that promote effective decision making.
MS Excel certification exam preparation. (Lec. 3) Pre: Open to students with a BU code earning a C- or better in MTH101, or by permission of the instructor.
FIN436X | Real Estate Development and Finance, effective Summer 2026 Add online modality to existing in-person course (3 crs.) The study of real estate development and finance with a focus on acquisition, finance, market analysis, design, and construction. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: FIN220 or FIN323, or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.

MKT265 | Marketing Principles, effective Summer 2026 Modify prerequisites (3 crs.) An introduction to marketing from a managerial viewpoint.
Examines social, economic, technological, legal, ethical, and other environmental factors and their impact on product, price, promotion, and distribution decisions in a worldwide market. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: Open to students with 24 credits or permission of dean's office.
COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDC316 | Foundations in Early Childhood Care & Education, effective Summer 2026 Change prerequisites, add accelerated online version (3 crs.) This foundational course prepares aspiring early childhood educators to develop their teaching philosophy, skills, and practices aligned with educational theories.
It emphasizes career exploration and commitment to the profession, promoting optimal learning for young children. (Lec. 3/Online/Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Admission to the College of Education or the Early Childhood Education Program, or Admission to the accelerated online early childhood care and education program, or by permission of instructor.

EDC474 | Early Childhood Practical Teaching Residency I, effective Fall 2026 Change title, description, number/level, credits, add accelerated online version (3 cr.) Students complete their initial residency experience in a public school PreK –3 classroom, attending two full days per week prior to Residency II.
Provides guided field experience supported by a clinical educator and a university supervisor.
Candidates apply developmentally appropriate practices, strengthen classroom management and assessment skills, and engage in reflective teaching to prepare for full-time student teaching in Residency II. (Practicum/Online/Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Concurrent enrollment in EDC426 and EDC475, Admission to College of Education; Admission to the Early Childhood Certification Program; Admission to the Early Childhood Care and Education for Working Professionals; or permission of the instructor.
S/U only.
COLLEGE OF NURSING: NUR203 | Comprehensive Health Assessment, effective Summer 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Introduces the techniques of history taking and systematic health assessment of individuals across the life span.
